title: HIDMaestro Controller Profile
description: Defines the identity and HID characteristics of a game controller for virtual device emulation.

vid.description: USB Vendor ID as hex string (e.g. '0x045E')

pid.description: USB Product ID as hex string (e.g. '0x028E')

productString.description: String returned by IOCTL_HID_GET_STRING (iProduct). This is what joy.cpl and games see.

manufacturerString.description: String returned for manufacturer query (iManufacturer). Null if unknown.

type.description: Device category. A mouse or keyboard profile delivers every input report in order, where a game controller sends the latest state, and gets no joy.cpl entry.

bluetoothTransport.description: v2.0.0, for connection 'bluetooth': the transport a real device of this kind uses, classic (BR/EDR, BTHENUM) or le (HID over GATT, BTHLEDevice). The devnode carries the hardware and compatible IDs a real device of that transport carries. Default classic.

bluetoothVendorIdSource.description: v2.0.0, for connection 'bluetooth': who assigned the VID, the USB-IF (usb, the default) or the Bluetooth SIG (bluetooth). It is the 0002 or 02 in front of the VID in the hardware IDs, 0001 or 01 for the SIG.

descriptor.description: HID report descriptor as a hex string (e.g. '05010905A101...'). Null if not yet captured.

inputReportSize.description: Length on the wire of the input report a data-only frame fills, in bytes, the report ID's byte included. The driver sends that report at this length. Null: the report's own length in the descriptor.

dataReportId.description: The input report a data-only frame (SubmitRawReport, and SubmitState's legacy path) fills and the driver sends it as, for a device where the SDK's own choice is wrong. The SDK lays out the first input report with gamepad fields, and for a keyboard or mouse the descriptor's first input report. Must name an input report the descriptor declares. Null: the SDK's choice.

deviceDescription.description: Device Manager display name (from vendor INF or Windows HID class). Null means use productString. This is what FriendlyName gets set to on the device node.

notes.description: Implementation notes, caveats, or special behavior.

nativeDescriptor.description: Record-keeping only: the descriptor read from the real device, kept verbatim beside the one the profile presents when the two differ. The loader reads it and no code uses it.

layout.description: Physical layout for consumer mapping/binding UIs: sticks, triggers, dpad, faceButtons, shoulderButtons, systemButtons, imu, haptics, etc. Bound to HMLayout (camelCase keys, case-insensitive).

buttonMap.description: Maps HMButton bit positions (array index) to descriptor button indices (value). Null = identity (Xbox layout). Sony profiles remap so A lands on Cross, X on Square, etc. -1 = this profile does not carry that button (the bit is dropped instead of falling through to identity). Values at or past the declared button count address the contiguous 1-bit vendor-page run that continues the button array, when the descriptor has one: the DualSense family declares 15 buttons then a 13x1-bit vendor field, and the Edge back paddles / Fn buttons live in its bits (value 16 = FnL 0x10 ... 19 = RB 0x80), matching where real firmware puts them without widening the descriptor.

triggerButtons.description: Button indices that represent digital trigger clicks (LT/RT as buttons).

axisMap.description: Maps HID usage (hex-string key) to a role name (e.g. 'leftTrigger'), overriding descriptor-derived axis roles. The names are leftStickX, leftStickY, rightStickX, rightStickY, leftTrigger and rightTrigger, in any case, and each usage is named once: a key in another spelling of a usage already named, or any other name, is refused.

axisCenters.description: The wire value a descriptor-path axis carries at 0.5, by axis name (X, Y, Z, Rz and the other HMAxis names), for a device whose hosts read its sticks at rest somewhere other than the field's midpoint. Each value lies inside its field's logical range. The field runs from its logical minimum at 0 through the center at 0.5 to its logical maximum at 1, each half on its own slope, rounded once as a distance from the center. The two Luna profiles set it, because SDL reads a Luna stick byte of exactly 0x7F as zero.

sdlMapping.description: SDL gamepad mapping body, everything after the GUID and name, trailing comma included. For pads SDL enumerates through DirectInput and has no database entry for, so it would otherwise expose them as roleless joysticks. Consumers prepend the runtime GUID and the profile name and call SDL_AddGamepadMapping.

triggerMode.description: Descriptor trigger encoding hint (e.g. 'combined', 'separate'). Describes wire encoding, not DirectInput presentation.

driverMode.description: 'xinputhid' binds Microsoft's xinputhid above the HID child. An alias for xinput.via 'xinputhid'.

xinput.description: v2.0.0: how the device reaches XInput and what its XUSB companion answers. Absent, the presentation comes from driverMode or the identity defaults (profiles/models/identity-defaults.json). An empty object means no XInput.

via.description: xusbCompanion: an XUSB companion devnode beside the HID device, as xusb22 presents a wired Xbox 360 pad. xinputhid: Microsoft's xinputhid binds above the HID child. Absent: no XInput.

subType.description: XINPUT_DEVSUBTYPE: gamepad (default), wheel, arcadeStick, flightStick, dancePad, guitar, guitarAlternate, drumKit, guitarBass, arcadePad, unknown, or a number 0 to 255 (decimal or 0x hex).

flags.description: The 36-byte GET_CAPABILITIES flags. Default voice and pmd. Give them here or in capabilities.flags.

battery.description: What GET_BATTERY_INFORMATION reports. Default wired, full.

information.description: The IDs GET_INFORMATION and GET_INFORMATION_EX carry and the companion's hardware ID takes, when they differ from the HID child's.

capabilities.description: The IDs and flags of the 36-byte GET_CAPABILITIES reply, when they differ from the HID child's and the block's.

driverPid.description: Override PID reported to the driver/companion when it must differ from the HID-attribute PID.

versionNumber.description: HidD_GetAttributes VersionNumber override. Sony DS4 BT ships 0 so Chromium selects the BT report layout.

sixaxisCompatible.description: v1.10.0: if true, the persona is a DualShock 3 presented the way Sony's sixaxis.sys and DsHidMini's SXS mode present one, which is what PCSX2 and RPCS3 read on Windows. The profile's extendedReport is the native 49-byte report 0x01 with alwaysArmed set. The driver serves it as the report 0 feature reply, derives the 12-byte joystick input report from it, and folds report 0 output commands into the native output report that extendedOutputReport decodes. See profiles/sony/dualshock-3-full.json.

inputDefaults.description: Fixed on-wire byte overlays applied after report build (e.g. DS5 Edge activeProfile status byte). Each entry is { byte, value }.

extendedReport.description: Data-driven vendor-blob INPUT spec (Sony BT Report 0x31/0x11, Switch 2 Pro Report 0x09, DualShock 3 Report 0x01): { reportId, size, armOn, alwaysArmed, fields[] }. Drives VendorBlobCodec.EncodeInput. armOn lists the host reads or writes that switch the pad into this report. With alwaysArmed set the report goes out from the first frame, for firmware that streams it from power-on.

extendedOutputReport.description: Data-driven vendor-blob OUTPUT spec (rumble/lightbar/triggers): { reportId, size, fields[] }. Drives VendorBlobCodec.EncodeOutput/Decode.

backend.description: Issue #39: which instantiation path creates this device. Absent or 'umdf2' is the default UMDF2 HID path most profiles use. 'usbip' marks a composite USB persona, which takes the USB/IP create path so it can present USB Audio Class interfaces alongside HID. That transport is bundled inside HIDMaestro.Core.dll and deploys itself on first use, so a usbip profile needs nothing installed by hand. A property of the device, never a mode toggle on an existing profile.

usbConfiguration.description: Issue #39: the USB configuration a composite persona presents (interfaces with alternate settings, isochronous endpoints, audio stream formats and channel roles). Only valid with backend 'usbip'. Shaped after the standard descriptor set so it can be authored from a real device's descriptor dump; see sdk/HIDMaestro.Core/Internal/UsbConfigurationSpec.cs for the field-level contract and profiles/sony/dualsense-composite.json for the authored example. Carries the wire truth verbatim: 'deviceDescriptor' (18-byte hex), 'configurationDescriptor' (full config blob hex, served byte-for-byte and cross-checked against the structured interfaces at create time), 'otherSpeedConfigurationDescriptor' (dual-speed devices only; its absence makes the backend stall Device_Qualifier and Other_Speed exactly as a single-speed real pad does), 'busSpeed' ('high' or 'full', the speed reported in the USB/IP import), and 'audioControls' (per feature unit: unitId, controlInterface, function, muteCur, and volumeMin/Max/Res/CurRaw as UAC1 s16 1/256-dB wire values, captured from a real pad's GET_MIN/MAX/RES/CUR exchanges, never invented). Issue #66: an interface of function 'vendor' may declare 'bulk' endpoints, which the backend serves for the persona that has a responder behind them (the Switch 2 Pro Controller) and stalls for any other. 'microsoftOs' carries the Microsoft OS 1.0 descriptors a device answers Windows with, as hex: 'string' (the 18 bytes read at string index 0xEE), 'extendedCompatId' and 'extendedProperties' (the feature descriptors a vendor request with wIndex 4 and 5 returns). With them Windows binds WinUSB to the interface they name with no driver install. A profile without the block stalls all three.

deviceModelFrom.description: v2.0.0: the device model the profile takes, by name, for the groups its own keys leave empty: the answers (featureStubs, valueSources), the protocol and the presentation (driverPid). It names a model the SDK carries (profiles/models), a model in the models folder of a directory a program loads, or a catalog profile. A name nothing holds, a named profile with no model, or a model that does not fit the profile's descriptor leaves the model the profile's identity gives it, and HMProfile.DeviceModelProblem says why.

deviceModel.description: v2.0.0: "none" takes no model by name or by the profile's identity, by the author's choice. The profile's own keys still apply. Refused beside deviceModelFrom, and the one value it takes is "none".

featureStubs.description: v2.0.0: the answers the device gives to GET_REPORT(Feature), one entry each in 'reports', on either backend. An entry is { id, size, data, patch, comment } and these keys: message { onReport, at, value } makes it answer only while the last SET on report onReport carried value (hex) at byte at, counted with the report ID byte. A param { at, value } narrows a message entry to one parameter byte, and an entry with an exact param is tried before one without. A pages list gives the answers a message entry gives in turn, the last repeating until a SET on onReport starts them again. A sizes list gives the lengths an answer comes in, served at the largest that fits the request. A minLength stalls a request shorter than it. An echo of true answers a message entry with the bytes of the SET it follows. A replyHead of 'requestReportId' puts the request's report ID in byte 0. A crc32 { seed } ends the answer with a CRC-32 over the seed and the answer's other bytes. A notify of true publishes the read to the program. Without notify an answer publishes on the usbip backend, as every answered GET did through v1.13.0, and does not on UMDF2. A GET is answered by a message entry whose message and param match, then one whose message matches, then a plain entry for its report ID, and else it stalls, as real hardware does for a request it does not implement. On a descriptor without report IDs every GET and SET is report 0. patch lists per-controller bytes, each { at, length, encoding, source, key, add }, where encoding is uint8, uint16-le, uint32-le, ascii or ascii-decimal and source is index, serial or a valueSources name. A model the profile takes by name or identity can carry the table instead (deviceModelFrom). The table-level match and messageByte of v1.x still load and expand to message entries. The steamFirmwareStamp key of v1.9.1 to v1.13.0 is refused: its stamp is a patch from a keyedHexFile value source. Limits: 64 entries, 64 bytes an answer, 16 pages, 4 reports carrying messages. See sdk/HIDMaestro.Core/Internal/Usbip/FeatureStubTable.cs, the Valve composites and profiles/models.

protocol.description: The device's protocol (docs/design/data-driven-devices.md, mechanism 3): registers (state), counters, memory images, the input endpoint and its clock, the commands and their rules, replies, decoders, halt, setProtocol, getStatus, getReport and the command log. On the usbip backend in this release. A value the load refuses is named by its JSON path.

stateBlock.description: The state a device that builds its own reports takes at SubmitState (mechanism 2): its size in bytes and its fields, in extendedReport's field vocabulary. A raw submit on such a device is a state block of this size.

inputReports.description: The reports a device builds from its state block (mechanism 2), each a layout: name, reportId, size, a while condition on the protocol's registers, send (clock, change or submit) and a program of ops (const, copy, bits, xor, swap16, field, lookup, hat8, pack12, counter, when). Two layouts may share a report ID only when their conditions cannot hold together.

liveFeatureReports.description: Feature reports a device builds from its state block when the host reads them (mechanism 2): reportId, size and a program.

stream.description: The idle repeat: the consumer's last frame sent again one period after the last frame went out, as the real device reports at rest. Replaces extendedReport.idleFrameIntervalMs, which still loads as a stream of that whole-millisecond period. A profile sets one of the two.

periodMs.description: The period in milliseconds, fractions allowed (1.25 for a DualSense over Bluetooth).

periodRegister.description: A protocol register the host sets the period through, times unitMs. While it holds 0 the period is periodMs.

while.description: A condition on the protocol's registers the repeat runs under, in the condition grammar: a string, or a list of terms that must all hold.

timestamps.description: hold, the default, repeats the frame's sensor timestamp. advance moves it on by the time since the frame, as the real device's clock does.

valueSources.description: v2.0.0: named per-controller values the patches of featureStubs read, beside the built-in index (the transport index) and serial (the serial the device serves). Each is { kind, roots, path }. The one kind, keyedHexFile, reads a KEY:HEX line of the file at path under the first of roots whose folder exists: a root is { registry: 'HKCU\\...' or 'HKLM\\...', value } naming a folder, or { knownFolder, path }. The key matches a whole line's key, an optional 0x and one to eight hex digits follow, and zero or an absent key leaves the captured bytes. The file is read when an answer is asked for, through a cache keyed on its last write time and length. Only valid with backend 'usbip': on UMDF2 the driver serves the answers without calling the SDK. steam-controller-2's steamUpdater source is Steam's hardwareupdater.cfg.

extendedField.description: One field of a vendor-blob report, the codec's vocabulary (sdk/HIDMaestro.Core/Internal/VendorBlobProgram.cs). Every normalized value is written as min + RoundHalfEven(v' x (max - min)) in double, v' the clamped input or 1 minus it with invert. A key a type ignores is refused when a create compiles the profile.

type.description: The field's wire form. In an output report, OutputDecoded carries a decoded field boxed as its type says: uint8, uint8-rolling, hat-octant and packed-uint box byte, uint8-axis and uint8-trigger box float, button-mask boxes List<string> of the pressed names, rgb24 boxes byte[3] and bytes-passthrough byte[]. No other type is decoded. packed-uint is an output type only. ds3-battery is refused: write uint8-level-map with its table.

byte.description: The byte the field is written at, the report ID's byte 0 included.

bytes.description: A byte range such as "3-8", for rgb24, bytes-passthrough, bytes-zero and crc32-le.

bits.description: A bit range such as "0-3" inside the byte, for bitfield, uint8-battery, hat-octant and button-mask.

semantic.description: The SDK value an input field reads, or the name an output field is reported under.

buttons.description: One name per bit: an HMButton name, "#n" for HMButton bit n, LT_DIGITAL, RT_DIGITAL, DPAD_UP, DPAD_DOWN, DPAD_LEFT, DPAD_RIGHT, LEFTPAD_TOUCH, RIGHTPAD_TOUCH, or "_" for an unused bit. A bitfield names flags.

center.description: uint8-axis: the wire value at rest, the range then running center - 127 to center + 127. uint10-be: the wire value at zero. int16-le: the wire value at zero, 0 to 65535, so 32768 writes offset binary.

min.description: The wire value at the SDK's 0 for uint8-axis, uint8-trigger, stick12-pair, int16-axis, int16-pad-or-stick's stick and uint16-trigger, and the no-contact value of uint16-pressure. Defaults to 0, or -32767 for the signed axes. Input reports only: an output field refuses it.

max.description: The wire value at the SDK's 1, and the contact value of uint16-pressure. Defaults to 255, 4095 or 32767 by the type's width. Required on uint16-trigger and uint16-pressure, where v1 wrote 32767 without it: give 32767 for v1's bytes or 65535 for the full width. Input reports only: an output field refuses it.

invert.description: The wire axis grows the other way from the SDK's, which runs 0 at the left and the top: on every axis and trigger type, the Y half of stick12-pair, and uint10-be. Required on an int16-axis, int16-pad or int16-pad-or-stick field of a Y semantic, which v1 negated without it: give true for v1's bytes. An output field takes it on uint8-axis only.

scale.description: int16-le of a calibrated source (accelGX to gyroDpsZ): counts per g or per degree per second, a number or an exact ratio [13371, 936]. In a packed-uint part, the value's factor.

negate.description: With scale: the calibrated value negated before it is scaled.

repeat.description: With scale: [count, stride], the field written count times, stride bytes apart.

dpad.description: button-mask with DPAD_* names, hat-octant: the d-pad from HatDegrees, then HatHundredths, then HatRaw, then Hat. Input reports only.

levels.description: uint8-level-map: the byte for each battery level from 0 to 10.

fullValue.description: uint8-battery: the level bits while full. uint8-level-map: the byte while full, ahead of chargingValue.

parts.description: packed-uint: the parts. Each part's value is assembled from its pieces, lowest first, in each frame, and the largest frame's value, plus offset, maps to 0 outside range and otherwise to itself times scale, rounded down or to nearest and clamped to 0..255. The field is the largest part's value, boxed as byte.

pieces.description: Bit groups: a bit offset from the report's first byte, its ID included, and a width. At most 32 bits in all.

frames.description: [count, stride]: the pieces read in count frames, stride bytes apart.

scope.description: crc32-le: the prefix bytes and the report bytes from and to the CRC covers.

clock.description: uint16-le, uint32-le sensorTimestamp: the field carries the codec's accumulator over divisor, modulo its width. The accumulator counts the controller's clock in 1/3 microsecond ticks until the first nonzero consumer stamp and the consumer's stamps from then on, adds the report's idleFrameIntervalMs for a stamp that restarted or ran backward, and the clock's time for a stamp of 0. It needs idleFrameIntervalMs.
